etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English fles, flees, flese, from Old English flēos, flīes, flȳs, from Proto-West Germanic *fleus.
senses: The hair or wool of a sheep or similar animal.
(uncountable) Insulating skin with the wool attached.
(transitive, informal) To con or trick (someone) out of money.
(transitive) To cut off the fleece from (a sheep or other animal).
